text:
maya: quick question — after the namespace-split terraform change, staging pods in `vector-ingest` are failing with KMS Decrypt AccessDenied. Any ideas?

maya: example error from pod logs: `AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt`

maya: infra bits we changed: we moved from a single grant to per-namespace grants keyed by `aws:PrincipalTag/namespace` and we now set `sts:SourceIdentity` in the IRSA role assume. snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "ingest" { ... }
resource "aws_kms_grant" "ingest_ns" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.ingest.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_vector_ingest.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      namespace = "vector-ingest"
    }
  }
}
```

ajay: hmm — two quick checks: 1) are the pods mounting the projected token (not the legacy token)? 2) is the `sts:SourceIdentity` value actually matching the tag/condition you're using in the grant? If SourceIdentity != tag value the key constraint would reject.

ajay: also run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <id>` in staging to confirm the grant exists and points at the right role ARN.

kevin: +1 to list-grants. I hit this once where terraform created the grant but the service account annotation got a different `service-account` name after a helm chart tweak so the role ARN changed. Plan looked fine because TF saw the old role as deleted and created a new one — but the grant creation race left a grant for the old ARN.

kevin: run `kubectl get sa -n vector-ingest -o yaml` and verify `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation matches the grant's grantee_principal.

maya: good call — SA annotation shows `arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/irsa-vector-ingest-2026`. list-grants shows grantee_principal = `arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/irsa-vector-ingest-2025` 😬

maya: so looks like TF applied a new role during the deploy and the grant didn't get updated with the new role. Is there a recommended pattern to avoid this race?

kevin: we usually do one of: 1) create the IAM role first and wait for annotations before creating the KMS grant; 2) use the KMS key policy to allow the `sts:AssumeRole` path (wider) instead of tight grants; or 3) create the grant with a wildcarded principal (not ideal). For automation I'd add an explicit k8s wait step after role creation so the SA annotation is stable before creating grants.

ajay: for Terraform ordering: make the IRSA role resource explicitly depend_on the helm release or k8s serviceaccount resource if TF manages both. If helm creates the SA outside TF, add a `null_resource` that runs `kubectl` check and use `local-exec` with `triggers` to serialize.

maya: i'll try adding a small CI gate: run `kubectl get sa` and validate annotation matches role ARN before granting. Also will add a `aws_kms_grant` lifecycle replace_when_role_changes = true? (no such arg, just thinking out loud)

kevin: there's no replace_when_role_changes but you can reference the role ARN directly so TF will see the dependency. If role is external, use a data resource for the IAM role and reference that — but that still can race if helm and tf run concurrently.

infra-bot: deploy-story: terraform apply finished in staging at 2026-03-03T14:20Z (plan ok, 3 resources changed).

maya: thanks all — i'll patch CI to wait for SA annotation and then re-run the grant apply. i'll post back after we validate decrypts. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: if this hits prod consider an emergency fallback: temporarily allow the key policy to permit the legacy role ARN or allow Decrypt for the staging role until we reconcile. Quick but audit noisy.

maya: noted. will avoid prod touch unless we see alerts.

maya: follow-up: after re-applying the grant with the correct grantee_principal, pods recovered immediately. leaving the CI wait in place.
